clause_evidence.reasoning: Every one of the 26 samples demonstrates subtraction through multiple pedagogical contexts: direct fill-in-the-blank calculation, inverse-of-addition framing, number line models, and error-detection evaluation, ensuring comprehensive illustration of the subtraction concept.

All 26 samples involve subtraction of a 1-digit number (ranging from 1 to 9) from a 2-digit number (ranging from 10 to 93), consistently maintaining the specified grade-level magnitude constraint for Grade 2 Quarter 2.

Eighteen of the 26 samples explicitly reference number line representations using language such as dot, move back, jump, or count back, but eight samples omit number line context, relying solely on inverse-of-addition framing or abstract problem statements without explicit number line visualization language.

Thirteen samples explicitly frame subtraction as the inverse of addition through hint statements or problem setup such as If 89 + 4 = 93, then 93 − 4 = 89 or Since 84 + 9 = 93, what is 93 − 9?, demonstrating and reinforcing this critical conceptual relationship throughout the packet.
